lines.english: "Why do Japanese trains have to be so crowded all the time?"
"You haven't been on enough overseas trains to compare in the first place. You almost never leave the house, and whenever you do, you take a taxi."
"I make sure to bring the receipts every time, don't I? You have no right to complain as my manager."
"Company funds are not a bottomless resource… You and your family should do something about your wastefulness."
"It's okay, that's what you and Miyo-chan are for. Touma Youko Office will be in safe hands as long as you two are around."
As the conversation strays further and further away from its initial purpose, the two of us look out the train windows at the nostalgic scenery outside.
It's the 30th of December. A few days after our return to Japan, and only two days before the year ends.
As always, we spend our time together without any idea of what the future holds in store for us, even on this sudden vacation.
"Iwazu-chou, Iwazu-chou. Please mind the door when exiting."
"Come on, let's get off. Quickly."
"I know. I get it, so can you please not pull my necktie? That's seriously dangerous."
"I'm amazed you still remember that."
"You must remember it yourself if you know what I was referring to."
"Getting caught up in memories?"
"Of course I am. I used this station all the time as a kid."
Just like the announcer said, we've arrived at Iwazu-chou.
The district Kazusa lived in until she graduated.
"Oh right, what should we get as a gift? We can't just go there empty-handed."
"I admire that you've become considerate enough to think about that, but you should've said that when we were in Onjuku.
"Haruki, you're underestimating convenience store candy. Unlike before, they sell plenty of souvenir-worthy goods now."
"You just want to buy it for yourself. Just admit it!"
And now…
I knew it from the beginning, but…
Seeing it with my own eyes leaves me speechless.
Because this house was once on the verge of turning into an abandoned ruin.
The nameplate was gone. There was a "for sale" sign at the front. The garden was overgrown.
"It really does… look like it used to."
"…It does."
But now, this place calls forth memories dating even further in the past.
Memories of the day I was astounded by the sheer size of the place.
Memories of the day I stepped inside, awestruck by how magnificent it was.
And lastly, memories of the day I felt feelings of admiration, respect, and sympathy for the single inhabitant of this place.
"Let's head in, shall we?"
"Yeah."
While still overwhelmed by all sorts of memories, we press the doorbell of what used to be her home.
…Even the sound of the doorbell is the same.
"Glad you made it, you two. It's been a while."
"We ate lunch together yesterday and the day before that."
"Come now, Kazusa, that was just business, a mere rite of passage, a teeny little appointment."
And the person who came to greet us is the current owner of this house.
Not that it wasn't always her home to begin with.
"You've really decided to move back here."
"I guess so. I never managed to sell it no matter how many years I waited."
It was only half a year ago that Youko-san decided to live in this house again.
It was undergoing renovations until just last month, and today is the big day she can finally show it to us.
Normally, Kudou-san and I would have been strongly opposed to a plan like this, writing it off as a "waste of money."
"It hasn't changed at all…"
"I made sure not to change anything. That only made the whole thing more expensive though."
The interior design is completely identical.
I only spent a few days in this house.
But even then, this scenery is so deeply ingrained in my memories that I instantly feel a wave of nostalgia.
"In truth, Miyo-chan lives with me here too, but since today is supposed to be 'family only,' she just got up and left to her parents' house on her own."
"She didn't have to be that considerate."
"Exactly. The only thing that awaits her at her parents' house is endless nagging about when she's getting married."
"How about you show some consideration too, in both your actions and your words."
Well, back then there certainly was no mother-daughter comedy duo around.
"What do you think?"
"…Not good, it's not sweet at all."
"How strange, I'm sure I put tons of sugar in it."
"How about we try adding in some maple syrup?"
"Oh dear, now it looks like liquid candy. Well, I suppose this is tasty in its own way…"
"No, when boiling black soybeans, you need to lower the temperature a bit… The peel will come off if you heat it up too much…"
"Shut up, armchair cook."
"I swear, all men are like this… They never do any cooking themselves, yet they're exemplary at complaining."
"I have more cooking experience than you two at least! So please let me help!"
This sparkly, newly renovated kitchen is being violated before my eyes.
A grossly sweet smell engulfs the whole room, and a white, almost sticky vapor spreads in the air.
Ingredients and spices lie scattered randomly on the table, and it's beyond anyone's ability to ever sort them back into their cabinets.
"Don't get in the way. New Year's osechi is something meant to be passed down from mother to daughter."
"But what is a mother meant to pass down when she hasn't inherited anything herself…?"
"To begin with, you were the one who said you wanted osechi for New Year's. You really are full of contradictions."
"I said I wanted osechi, yes, but I never said I wanted you two to make it…"
This was the inevitable result, after all.
I'm certain they'll both be sick of this when cleaning up is all that's left.
"You can just go take a nap for now. I'll wake you up when it's time for dinner."
"Fine…"
This amount of suspense can't be good for my mental health, so I should take my leave for now. I can do all my lamenting later.
"Oh? The sweetened chestnuts for the kuri kinton are gone… Hey, Kazusa!"
"I didn't eat them all, just so you know! I made sure to leave two."
"Same here. I made sure to only eat five."
I was sure they'd at least finish preparing a meal sooner or later, but perhaps I was being too optimistic.
"Ah…"
Going down the stairs to the basement, I open a door many times thicker than a normal one…
Beyond that door is a scenery that's completely unchanged from before.
In one of the corners of this soundproofed and all too spacious studio stands a piano belonging to Kazusa's favorite brand.
From guitars to drums to saxophones… All kinds of instruments lie piled on the floor in a heap.
Even the control room beyond the big soundproof glass looks like it's equipped with new hardware.
…Even though there's no guarantee anyone will ever use it.
This obsession of restoring this house down to the smallest details brings out a slightly bewildered smile on my lips.
Years ago, when I was still a high school student.
There was no one in this room but a lone, embittered girl all by herself.
And although that girl seemed completely unconcerned about others, she made an exception for a guy who couldn't properly play an instrument.
She brought the good-for-nothing guy who wouldn't take music seriously to this room, where she played for him, made him play, and verbally abused him…
And she stuck with him until he was ready for an actual performance.
That's why that good-for-nothing guyーwhy Iーended up relying on that strict girl, why I wanted to be spoiled by her, and why I refused to leave her side.
I came to this room countless times, played in it countless times, dozed off in it countless times, and greeted the morning in it countless times.
And then after five long years, my dream came true.
My nearly impossible dream of being on good terms with this bitter girl.
"Oh, you were in here."
"Ah…"
The second I heard her voice, I clumsily put the guitar back on its stand.
"Wow… I'm amazed she went as far as to restore this place."
"Y-Yeah…"
But Kazusa pretends to not have seen that unnatural movement.
It's just a guess… but it's probably because Kazusa understands the reason why I can never play the guitar in front of her.
"Wow, she's even tuned this thing. That woman is nothing if not meticulous."
But Kazusa doesn't breathe a word about that, instead opting to stroke the keys of the piano with a hint of nostalgia.
"Feeling nostalgic again?"
"Well, it's all nostalgic to some degree, but this is the one place in Japan where I spent the most time."
"I see… I guess you're right."
The piano that once stood in this room now rests in Vienna, always by Kazusa's side.
Even so, Kazusa greets this new piano with the same expression she would show the original.
"Ah, by the way, Haruki, it's time for dinner soon. I only came down here to let you know that the pizza just arrived."
"…Weren't you two preparing something just earlier?"
"You poor ignorant soul. Osechi is for New Year's Day. What would be the point in eating it before New Year's?"
"What's wrong with a single bite?"
"You can do that tomorrow… I'll try making it properly this time."
"…Actually, never mind."
"Alright, I'll be sleeping in the guest room."
Three people sitting around the dinner table of the Touma household, cheerfully passing the time by watching a lame variety TV show,
Just like that, these three were able to waste their time in happiness and quiet, in a way that seemed impossible just a few months prior.
But despite that, or perhaps because of that, this precious time passed by in a flash, and the needle of the table clock began to inch closer to midnight.
Inching closer to the final day of the year.
"What do you mean? You could just stay here. If you get sleepy we can all just huddle together."
"No, you two should have some time for yourselves, as mother and daughter."
"Huuh? You don't want to stay? You can prey on either of us, I wouldn't mind."
"I would mind, Mom…"
"Wow, she's actually taking it seriously. My daughter is so lame."
Even with New Year's right around the corner, the Touma comedic duo knows no bounds.
"Anyway, Kazusa, see you tomorrow."
"I'll come over in the morning."
"Got it. Good night."
"Yeah."
After enjoying my fill of alcohol and a good meal, I leave the living room with a sense of relief, exasperation, and the slightest hint of jealousy.
It's almost time. Time for the last day of the year. And most importantly, it's time for…
"Seriously, you two get along so well it's almost annoying… You really know how to ensnare the right kind of man."
"That's not true at all. He's stingy, loud, annoying, and all around terrible."
"Hmmm?"
"It's just that… he's the only man for me."
"…Unlike what you just did, I don't think I've ever laid all my cards bare for my man to see."
"Why not?"
"Well, you know, love is… Goodness, maybe I really have raised you improperly."
"…Haah."
"Want another glass?"
"You should make this your last one, Mom."
"Then how about we go to sleep? In the same bed."
"…You didn't even let me do that when I was a kid. Why are you trying to act like a good parent all of a sudden?"
"You've got it all wrong. This is simply me manipulatively trying to act nice so that the child I abandoned will take care of me when I grow old."
"That's right, I'm manipulative. That's why I prepared this house for you two to return to."
"So that really was… the reason you returned to this house."
"You can return whenever you want. I'm serious."
"Mom…"
"Besides, this is a chance for you two, don't you think?"
"A chance for what?"
"You know, even if my illness were to heal, it's still obvious that I'll die before you do… Then you'll inherit this house without having to pay for it."
"The only thing I can imagine is the crippling inheritance tax."
"And to solve that issue, you have a beloved husband who will earn back that money by raising sheep or something."
"Hey, just to make sure, you're not referring to anyone in specific when you say 'sheep,' right?"
"…! No, I really can't."
"Why not? This is where you were born."
"You know already, don't you? There is a reason why the two of us were never supposed to come here in the first place…"
"There isn't! …Not anymore."
"Mom…?"
"There is no such reason for either of you anymore. You've both been forgiven for a long time."
"B-But… I'm…"
"I went over countless times."
"Huh…?"
"In the beginning, they wouldn't even see me. It was only after the fifth attempt that they let me into their house."
"Mom…?"
"I don't remember how many times I met them after that, but eventually their daughter helped me to convince them as well."
"What were you doing…?"
"That's what I should be asking you, really."
"Why would you do something like that, Mom…?"
"Well, obviously, a mother has to apologize for her daughter's mistakes."
"You shouldn't be the one to do that, Mom. I'm an adult now, aren't I?"
"No matter how old you get, you'll always remain my child. Not to mention that in your case, mental age needs to be considered as well."
"I have to say though, it was the first time in a long time, or perhaps the first time ever, that I truly felt like a parent."
"Idiot… You idiot…!"
"Anyway, that's how it is… In other words, there's no reason to deny my request any longer."
"Uu, uah…!"
"That's why, Kazusa… please come back here whenever you want, okay…?"
"Even if you're only coming back to play a concert here, celebrate Obon or New Year's, or simply coming to visit some old friends. That's enough for me."
"And, and… if you ever feel the slightest bit homesick, don't hesitate to come back."
"Mom… Mom…!"
"What is it? Are you sleepy already? Then let's go to sleep together."
"No… First I want to…"
"Huh?"
"Mom…"
"H-Huh?"
"Thank you for… raising me."
"…Pfff! Hah… hahaha!"
"W-Why are you laughing?"
"B-Because! 'The' Kazusa just went on her knees, bowed… and said 'Thank you for raising me!'"
"You're the one who did something unlike you first!"
"But, but, but…! Aahaha, ahahahaha!"
"Shut up, shut up! I'll never forget what you did for me, just so you know!"
"Me… Me neither…! I'll never forget the look of you just earlier for the rest of my life. Ahahahahaha… Aaah, ahahaha…!"
"Mom, you idiot…! Uaaah… Hahaha…!"
